ageing_relevance.rationale: B2M is a GrimAge plasma-protein component and ~10% of its papers concern ageing, but Open Targets lists no ageing-disease associations. The project's DNAm surrogate is not a measured protein level, and the schizophrenia effect was explained by smoking.

evidence.value: One of seven plasma proteins whose DNA-methylation surrogates make up GrimAge, the mortality clock that was +4.3 years older in schizophrenia in part 1 of this project (an effect explained by smoking). The surrogates are methylation estimates, not measured protein levels.

background_knowledge: Circulating B2M rises with age and has been reported in rodent studies to impair cognition and neurogenesis; it also predicts mortality in human cohorts.

mechanism.rationale: B2M's function is well defined as the MHC-I light chain. Its causal role in ageing is less clear. Inhibiting circulating B2M is the likely direction, but B2M is needed for MHC-I antigen presentation.

evidence.value: Component of the class I major histocompatibility complex (MHC). Involved in the presentation of peptide antigens to the immune system.

background_knowledge: Free circulating B2M is a proposed pro-ageing factor in parabiosis studies; the evidence is mostly preclinical.
B2M forms amyloid in dialysis-related amyloidosis.

tractability.rationale: Small-molecule evidence shows a ligand-bound structure and a high-quality pocket. Antibody tractability is supported by the protein being secreted and cell-surface, and PROTAC evidence exists. There is no clinical-stage modulator, and no 'other modality' evidence.

safety.rationale: Open Targets lists no liabilities, but absence of data is not evidence of safety. B2M is essential for MHC-I surface expression, so systemic inhibition risks immune deficiency.
background_knowledge: Loss-of-function B2M causes MHC-I deficiency and immune evasion in tumours. B2M knockout mice have iron overload and impaired CD8 T-cell development.

clinical_precedence.rationale: No drugs are listed for B2M.

assessment.summary: B2M is the MHC-I light chain and a secreted plasma protein. It is one of the seven GrimAge surrogate proteins. About 10% of its literature concerns ageing, but Open Targets has no ageing-disease associations. Its top disease links are MHC-I deficiency, lymphoma and amyloidosis. The project's GrimAge link rests on DNA-methylation surrogates, and the schizophrenia signal was explained by smoking. It is moderately tractable (small-molecule pocket, antibody and PROTAC features) but has no clinical candidates. The main concern is safety: B2M is essential for MHC-I antigen presentation, so any inhibition would need to target the circulating pool selectively. Overall it is a "consider" target, mainly as a biomarker, with a mechanistic hypothesis that still needs validation.
key_uncertainties: Whether circulating B2M is causal in ageing or only a biomarker; the evidence is mostly preclinical background knowledge, and the DNAm surrogate is not a measured protein level
Whether the free circulating pool can be selectively reduced without disrupting MHC-I function
No clinical candidates and no Open Targets ageing-disease associations
Safety data are absent, not shown to be clean
